title: model-agnostic measurements (shift clustering, restricted shifts, entropy floor)
hypothesis: the ciphertext+cribs carry model-agnostic structure that constrains the cipher
insights: (1) Shift-as-fn-of-plaintext: a single 26-entry shift table T (per-letter median) satisfies 8/24 cribs exactly, 12/24 within |delta|<=1, 16/24 within <=2. Per-letter spread (max-min) for multi-occurrence letters: {'E': 19, 'A': 1, 'S': 1, 'T': 23, 'N': 3, 'O': 15, 'R': 0, 'L': 4, 'C': 3}.
(2) The 24 cribs use 14/26 distinct shift values [0, 1, 2, 6, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20, 23, 24, 25]; fixed points (shift 0) at positions [33, 74]; P(<= 14 distinct by chance under uniform) = 0.191.
(3) Free-positions (73) unigram entropy = 4.332 bits; monoalphabetic-English-at-N p99 = 3.885, frac of English samples with entropy >= K4's = 0.000. Best autocorrelation offset = 7 (9 coincidences).

CONSTRAINT: K4's free-position entropy (4.33) exceeds the monoalphabetic-English null (p99=3.88) -- a flatness bound proving a polyalphabetic/fractionating stage is required (lower bound on period/order, analogous to chi=3).
next_steps: if shift-table fit strong: solve T over free positions and verify; use the entropy floor to set the minimum period in any future polyalphabetic sweep
